text: Prevalent means very common. Here, knee pain is so common among runners that it has its own name.
Resilient means able to take stress and bounce back. Here, slow training makes tendons and bones tougher so they handle running.
A novice is a beginner who is still learning. Here, new runners report injuries more often than experienced ones.
Arthritis is a sickness that makes joints swollen, stiff, and sore. Here, people worry that running for years will cause it, but the study found no link.
A tendon is a tough cord that joins a muscle to a bone. Here, using tendons a little more each week makes them thicker and stronger.
A term of art is a special phrase that people in one field all know and use. Here, runner's knee is such a common problem that it became one.
Runner's knee is an ache around the kneecap that many joggers get.
The kneecap is the small, round bone at the front of your knee.
An assortment is a mix of different kinds of things. Here, runner's knee is just one of many kinds of injury.
An overuse injury happens when you do too much of an activity without enough rest, so the body cannot heal in time.
Tolerable means possible to put up with. Here, a little training at a time is fine, but the total can add up to too much.
Cumulatively means adding up bit by bit over time. Here, small amounts of running pile up into a load that is too heavy.
To compound means to make something get worse by piling more on top. Here, one injury can lead to another.
Odds are how likely something is to happen. Here, an earlier injury made another one 62% more likely.
To wear down means to slowly use something up until it is thin or weak.
To keep something at bay means to hold it off so it cannot reach you. Here, runners want to keep injuries away.
A review is a study that gathers and compares the results of many other studies.
Susceptibility means how easily something can be harmed. Here, it is how likely a runner is to get hurt.
An adage is an old saying that people say is wise. Here, it is "slow and steady."
Slow and steady means going carefully at an even pace. It comes from the idea that the tortoise beats the hare.
An epidemiologist is a scientist who studies how health problems spread and who gets them.
A twinge is a quick, small pain that comes and goes.
Seasoned means experienced. Here, a seasoned runner has been running for a long time.
Sprinters are runners who race at top speed over short distances. Here, it just means runners.
Associated with means linked to. It shows two things go together but does not prove one causes the other.
To adapt means to change so you fit new conditions. Here, the body slowly grows stronger when the load rises gently.
Collagen is a stringy material in your body that makes skin, tendons, and bones strong.
To stiffen means to become harder and less bendy. Here, it makes tendons stronger.
Strain is a pushing or pulling force on something. Too much strain can hurt it.
Osteoblasts are tiny cells that build new bone.
A stress fracture is a tiny crack in a bone caused by being hit again and again.
Cartilage is the smooth, rubbery cushion between bones at a joint.
The shinbone is the long bone in the front of your lower leg.
Bone mineral density tells how packed and strong your bones are. Higher is stronger.
Resistance training is exercise that makes muscles work against a weight, like lifting.
Cumulative means the total of everything added together.
Body-mass index is a number doctors figure from weight and height to estimate body size.
Persistent means lasting a long time and not going away.
A marathon is a very long running race of about 26 miles (42 kilometers).
The long run is a pun here. It means both a long-distance run and a long stretch of time.
Evidence-based means built on facts and test results rather than guesses.
